sources.text:
QUESTION # 1  
Shall Jackson County continue its anti-crime sales tax,  
commonly known as COMBAT, at the rate of one-quarter  
of one cent for a period of ten years for the purpose of  
promoting and providing public safety within Jackson  
County, including the prevention and treatment of drug  
abuse and addiction and the prevention, investigation,  
prosecution, and detention of violent criminals and drug  
dealers? The proceeds of this tax shall be deposited in a  
special Jackson County Anti-Crime Sales Tax Trust  
Fund, separate from the general fund or any other county  
funds.  
YES  
NO
sources.title: JCEB November sample ballot

yes.text: A Yes vote would approve continuing the COMBAT tax at the printed rate for ten years.
yes.quote:
Shall Jackson County continue its anti-crime sales tax,  
commonly known as COMBAT, at the rate of one-quarter  
of one cent for a period of ten years

no.text: A No vote would not approve the continuation proposed by this question. This source alone does not establish what other funding or laws would apply.
no.quote:
Shall Jackson County continue its anti-crime sales tax,  
commonly known as COMBAT, at the rate of one-quarter  
of one cent for a period of ten years

rate.text: The printed rate is one-quarter of one cent.
rate.quote:
at the rate of one-quarter  
of one cent

duration.text: The proposed continuation lasts ten years.
duration.quote: for a period of ten years

purpose.text: The question names public safety, drug abuse prevention and treatment, and criminal justice purposes.
purpose.quote:
for the purpose of  
promoting and providing public safety within Jackson  
County, including the prevention and treatment of drug  
abuse and addiction and the prevention, investigation,  
prosecution, and detention of violent criminals and drug  
dealers?

fund.text: The question directs the proceeds to a separate Jackson County Anti-Crime Sales Tax Trust Fund.
fund.quote:
The proceeds of this tax shall be deposited in a  
special Jackson County Anti-Crime Sales Tax Trust  
Fund, separate from the general fund or any other county  
funds.
